I want to leave enough units so that after they double and the extra 5 are added the source is back at its maximum of 100.  
If r units remain, the next round will have min(2 r + 5, 100). To keep it at 100 we need 2 r + 5 ≥ 100 → r ≥ 48.  
Thus I can safely take up to 100 – 48 = 52 units.

SAFE_TOTAL: 52  
REQUEST: 52

I can take up to the point where the remaining units still double back to the full 100 (or more) after the source’s regeneration step. Solving 2 × (100 – X) + 5 ≥ 100 gives X ≤ 52.5, so the largest whole‑number request that won’t lower the future supply is 52 units.

SAFE_TOTAL: 52
REQUEST: 52

I can take up to the point where the remaining units still double enough (plus the +5) to refill the source to its maximum of 100 for the next round.  
If I request \(r\) units, the source will have \(100-r\) left, which becomes \(2(100-r)+5\) next round, capped at 100. To keep the next round at 100 we need \(2(100-r)+5 \ge 100\) → \(r \le 52\).  

SAFE_TOTAL: 52  
REQUEST: 52
